context:
Goal: claude-settings merges resume without hiding a real failure.
Problem (rule): main's last push run is red on one page test (dismiss focus, from #1308) that passed 3 of 3 other runs on the same code. The merge tool refuses every batch on a red main; --base-red-ok is for "the batch that carries the fix". Fix PR #1405 does not fix the cause (unknown; the code moves focus at once). It makes the next failure name where focus went, and files step dismiss-focus-root-cause. Whether that counts as the fix batch is your call.
Based on (test): main push run 42357626483 failed twice; schedule run 42363147772, the PR run and a branch dispatch passed.
Based on (read): merge/merge.py RED_FLAG: --base-red-ok is "the way out for the batch that carries the fix".
Departs from: main lets only a batch that fixes the red merge onto it — this once, a batch that instruments a flaky test and files its follow-up may too.
home: batch runner 8 merges or holds; step dismiss-focus-root-cause

options.gain: About 10 waiting PRs move today; the next red names its cause.
options.label: Runner 8 merges #1405 alone with --base-red-ok; the queue resumes on main's next push run
options.lose: Main merges once onto a red run whose cause is unknown. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.

options.gain: The flag keeps its narrow meaning.
options.label: Hold the queue until the root cause is found and fixed (recommended)
options.lose: Every claude-settings merge waits, for an unmeasured time.

reply: Routed 06:30 CST to the coordinator. The merge queue holds until step dismiss-focus-root-cause finds and fixes the cause; #1406 does not merge on red main under --base-red-ok.
short: cs main red: merge #1405 or hold
title: claude-settings main is red on a flaky test: merge #1405 onto it with --base-red-ok, or hold every merge?
why: Every claude-settings merge waits on this. Meanwhile the queue stays held and lane dismiss-focus-main-red finishes #1405's review round 2.
